audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer notices that Dominus (R) grants Renekton bonus Health while Zac's Unstable Matter (W) deals a percentage of the target's maximum health as magic damage. Both layers treat his ult as a pure threat to run from.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it points the opposite way to the current advice. Renekton ulting inflates the exact stat Zac's W scales against, so a Zac with W up gets stronger the moment Dominus comes on. The current text tells the player to disengage at 6, which throws away his best %max-HP window. W is on a flat 5s cooldown, so it lands repeatedly inside a Dominus duration.
audit.corrected: Dominus gives Renekton bonus Health for its duration. Unstable Matter (W, 5s flat) takes a percentage of his maximum health, so his ult raises your W damage. Do not reflexively disengage at 6 — check your own HP and anti-heal first.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (Unstable Matter: 'a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage', cooldown 5)

audit.whatIsWrong: content spikes[1].text writes the ability as 'a Dice (E) gap-close'. The ability is Slice and Dice.
audit.why: A truncated ability name reads as a different spell and undermines trust in the rest of the entry. The same file writes it correctly in wants.foe[1], so this is an isolated typo, not a naming convention.

audit.whatIsWrong: full breakdown.cooldowns says only 'Empowered = long stun. E-knock it. Track it before every engage' with no numbers, and content never states a single cooldown for him.
audit.why: The whole entry is built on 'trade around Ruthless Predator' but never says how long the window is. Ruthless Predator is 16s at rank 1 — one of the longest basic cooldowns Zac faces in the top lane — and the stun is 0.75s unempowered versus 1.5s at 50+ Fury. Those are two completely different trades and the player needs the actual numbers to pick one.
audit.corrected: Ruthless Predator 16/14/12/10/8s; 0.75s stun raw, 1.5s at 50+ Fury. Slice and Dice 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. Cull the Meek 7s flat and it heals him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/renekton.json (cooldowns and stun durations from Riot Data Dragon)

audit.whatIsWrong: Reign of Anger (P) generates Fury faster when Renekton is low on life. Nothing in either layer mentions it, and both push a 'finish him' pattern late in trades.
audit.why: It inverts the normal read on a low-HP enemy. A Renekton at 25% health refills his Fury bar faster than one at full, so the moment he looks killable is also the moment his empowered W stun comes back online. That is exactly when a Zac who has spent E and R walks in and dies.
audit.corrected: Low-HP Renekton builds Fury faster, so the empowered 1.5s stun is most likely precisely when he looks finishable. Commit only with Q and W available, not just because his bar is low.
sources: champ-data/_kits/renekton.json (Reign of Anger: 'Fury, increased when he is low on life')

audit.why: The full layer already carries anti-heal in Itemization and breakdown.late, which matches the _missing-interactions 'needs-antiheal' flag for Cull the Meek. The content layer had no mention, so I added the timing there rather than duplicating it in full.
audit.corrected: Cull the Meek heals on a 7s flat cooldown and more at 50+ Fury; Grievous Wounds before your two-item window is what makes the scaling plan actually arrive.
sources: champ-data/_kits/renekton.json (Cull the Meek, cooldown 7, heal flag)

notes: Best find here: Dominus grants bonus Health and Zac's Unstable Matter deals %maximum health, so Renekton's ultimate makes Zac's W hit harder — both layers currently tell the player to disengage at 6, which is backwards. Second: Reign of Anger generates Fury faster at low health, so the moment Renekton looks killable is the moment his 1.5s empowered stun returns; nothing in the data warned about that. Also fixed a truncated ability name ('a Dice (E)' -> Slice and Dice). The suspectNames flag on wants.foe[1] ('Use Slice and Dice') is a FALSE POSITIVE — the name is correct, the detector matched on the leading 'Use '. Left alone: full.diffRating 7.5/10 vs a 48.86% win rate over 219 games is roughly consistent, and the level chart (Renekton 6/7, Zac at two items) matches a sub-50% early-dominant lane, so I made no chart changes. One intended edit was dropped: full dontsFull[1].t ('Get empowered-W stunned') appears twice verbatim in zac.full.js, so the applier cannot target it unambiguously — the low-HP Fury warning went into phases[3].why instead.
